title.narrative: Output 7.1. Increased capacity of Member States to ensure respect for, promote and realize fundamental principles and rights at work

description.narrative: Following the launch of the NAP on12th June 2021, the Government of Uganda took measures to operationalize the NAP through the inauguration of the National Steering Committee on Elimination of Child Labour. The committee of 35 members is drawn from 21 institutions/organisations i.e., Government Ministries, CSOs and UN agencies. Employing resources availed under the Netherlands’, ministry of foreign affairs project on Accelerating action for the elimination of child labour in supply chains in Africa (ACCEL Africa- RAF/18/08/NLD), the ILO supported the government of Uganda to operationalize her National Action Plan on Elimination of Child Labour (NAP II 2020/21 – 2024/25) which was developed and adopted in the last biennium. The ILO support was delivered at National and District Local Government levels. At the national level, the Child Labour National steering committee which is the Institutional governance mechanisms for coordination and implementation of the NAP was supported to perform its functions, including that of the Child Labour Unit which is its Secretariat in the Ministry of Gender, Labour, and Social Development. Five quarterly national steering committee meetings were conducted in this the biennium. Specifically, the following activities were implemented to operationalize the NAP, led by the Government through the Ministry of Gender Labour and Social Development (MGLSD); 1) 100 lower District local governments (Education, Agriculture, Health, Community Development, Probation and Welfare, and employers, and workers representatives trained on handling of child labour issues, 2) Training of ILO constituents (28 officials) on International Labour Standards reporting included responding to comments raised by the Committee of Experts on the Application of Standards. 3) 32 child labour inspections conducted and 7 joint child labour monitoring visits 4) Support for stakeholder workshop to review and prepare progress report to comply with reporting obligation under the A 8.7 pathfinder countries. (Uganda is a member), 5) Federation of Uganda Employers was supported to develop a Training package on Child Labour Due Diligence for companies in the Tea and Coffee supply chain.

Output 7.4. Increased capacity of Member States to provide adequate labour protection to workers in diverse forms of work arrangements, including on digital labour platforms, and in informal employment

description.narrative: In September 2023, the government in consultation with the social partners, validated a country-level diagnosis on the penetration of digital labour platforms across different sectors of the economy. The diagnosis documented the experiences of workers, with a focus on women in accessing and performing work on such platforms in the Ugandan economy, as well as the decent work deficits for women and men on digital labour platforms. The diagnosis was developed in consultation with social partners. The surveys were based on the sectors validated by the ILO’s tripartite constituents in September 2021 and included taxi, delivery, domestic work, e-commerce, and online platform work (freelance). With support from the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation (BMGF), ILO conducted a survey of 850 workers across the identified sectors of the Ugandan economy and also conducted key informant interviews with representatives of governments, trade unions, employers’ organizations and platform companies to capture their perspectives, particularly regarding public policies frameworks to promote decent work in the platform economy. The country-level diagnosis serves to enhance the capacities of the ILO’s tripartite constituents regarding the penetration of digital labour platforms across various sectors in the economy and also highlights the opportunities and challenges for workers performing tasks on these platforms. The diagnosis will contribute towards the ongoing debate regarding reviewing and reforming the Employment Act 2006, and to adopt policies that would ensure that workers on digital labour platforms are protected. It will also help towards formulating job creation policies in Uganda, in light of the increasing educated youth unemployment in the country.
